title: Reading a level before your crew commits
target: How to read a R.E.P.O. level as it is generated, so the crew picks a direction early instead of drifting from room to room until the timer runs out.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A crew already inside a run
A way to talk to each other
Enough carrying space for what you expect to find

steps.do: Learn the opening rooms before anyone splits off on their own.
steps.because: a level is generated in a fixed order that begins with the start room (LevelState)

steps.do: Work out whether this level holds enemies at all before you commit to a fight.
steps.because: a level carries a note about whether it has enemies (HasEnemies)

steps.do: Treat a dead end as a decision rather than an accident.
steps.because: the level description names dead-end modules alongside the normal and passage ones (ModulesDeadEnd1)

steps.do: Find the extraction point and its area before you fill both arms.
steps.because: the extraction point is a placed thing with an area of its own (ExtractionPoint)

steps.do: Check what this level prefers to hold before deciding what is worth carrying out.
steps.because: a level carries its own preferred set of valuables (ValuablePresets)

commonMistakes: Splitting up before anyone has seen the start room.
Filling both arms before you know where the extraction point is.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
